episodes.180433: Clusters of thunderstorms, a couple of which were strong to severe, developed during the mid afternoon hours and lingered into the early evening hours across north central Alabama. A few reports of wind damage were received in Colbert, Lawrence and Madison Counties.
episodes.180475: A backdoor front entered northeastern NM during the early morning hours increasing surface moisture across the region. This added moisture along with daytime heating allowed isolated supercells to develop across southeastern Colfax and eastern Mora counties, moving southeast towards the Texas state line. Storms produced up to golf ball sized hail in Springer and near Roy, and wind gusts of up to 74 mph at Tucumcari.
episodes.180510: Strong thunderstorms moving offshore produced wind gusts and a waterspout in Brevard County.
episodes.180524: Scattered storms formed ahead of an approaching cold front during the afternoon and evening of July 6, 2023. A few of the cells merged to form a short-lived line that produced sporadic wind damage and a measured gust to 58 mph at Williamsport Regional Airport.
episodes.180775: A weak upper level trough extended southwest from the Great Lakes Region southwest into Southwest Arkansas and Northeast Texas during the afternoon of July 6th, which reinforced a weak surface front south into the I-30 corridor of Northeast Texas and Southern Arkansas. Meanwhile, a strong seabreeze pushed inland across East Texas and North Louisiana during the late afternoon through the evening hours, allowing showers and thunderstorms to spread north into these areas. Strong daytime heating and large scale ascent along the slow moving front contributed to the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms along and south of the front across portions of East Texas and North Louisiana, and collided with the northward advancing storms associated with the seabreeze during the late afternoon and early evening hours, with a cluster of showers and thunderstorms redeveloping over the same areas from Harrison County Texas into Southern Caddo and Bossier Parishes in Northwest Louisiana. Given the very moist air mass in place, these slow moving storms were efficient rainfall producers, contributing to areas of flash flooding that were observed over these locations. Localized pockets of 2-5 inch rains fell over the city of Marshall in Central Harrison County in a short period of time, with multiple roads flooded before the storms diminished by mid and late evening.
episodes.180805: A severe thunderstorm moved east-northeast out of northern Colorado into Cheyenne County Nebraska south of Sidney on the evening of the 5th with up to half dollar size hail.
episodes.181253: A strong summer time subtropical ridge was located over southern New Mexico with a weak short wave moving over the top of the ridge. Low level upslope flow combined with weak large scale lift creating an isolated storm in the extreme southeastern Texas Panhandle late on the fifth. Additional thunderstorm activity formed on the higher terrain of New Mexico and drifted into West Texas early in the morning on the sixth. A strong outflow boundary ahead of the complex of thunderstorms produced severe wind gusts for several hours as it progressed from the extreme southwestern Texas Panhandle into the central South Plains.
episodes.181568: Summer thunderstorms developed across primarily south central and southwestern Montana in early July. Several of these storms produced large hail and strong gusty winds. The strongest storms impacted the Bozeman area and Canyon Ferry Lake recreational area.
episodes.181707: Westerly flow pushed sea breeze storms offshore of the local Atlantic coast in the afternoon and early evening.
episodes.181708: Westerly flow pushed sea breeze storms offshore of the local Atlantic coast in the afternoon and early evening.
episodes.181868: Unstable air along a pressure trough well ahead of a cold front over the Ohio River Valley sparked scattered thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours. Localized wind damage was reported in northern Maryland, and a considerably severe thunderstorm affected parts of the central Shenandoah Valley in Virginia.
episodes.182028: A Seabreeze thunderstorm over Sumter County resulted in a lightning strike that caused a fire in the attic and damage to the water main.
episodes.182164: Despite a rather nebulous upper air pattern, a weak impulse instigated deep convection across western-north Texas. Sufficient wind shear and instability allowed for at least transient storm organization. The strongest storms produced severe-caliber wind gusts and wind damage across the area.
episodes.182165: A mesoscale convective system (MCS) moved into parts of northwestern Oklahoma early on the morning of the 6th. While generally weak/unsupportive magnitudes of wind shear and instability lead to its gradual decay across the area, a severe-caliber wind gust was measured in Ellis County.
episodes.182724: Thunderstorms in Minnesota lead to some lightning damage in northwestern Minnesota.
episodes.182971: A surface trough located along the eastern North Carolina Piedmont led to the development widely isolated scattered showers and thunderstorms in the late afternoon and evening hours. A few of the storms became severe, with downed power lines and trees in Cumberland and Alamance counties.
episodes.183006: A typical summer pattern prevailed with scattered thunderstorms producing occasional gusty winds across the coastal waters.
episodes.183060: Several rounds of thunderstorms impacted the combined OK/TX Panhandles during the early evening hours of the 5th and going through into the early AM hours of the 6th. First, in the eastern TX Panhandle. Then a complex came in from eastern New Mexico impacting the southwestern TX Panhandle. Another complex then came in from SE Colorado and SW Kansas impacting the northern combined OK/TX Panhandles. Severe winds occurred with these storms and one instance of 1 hail also occurred. The strongest winds were with the complex that came into the OK Panhandle with winds upwards of 70 to 80 mph. The storms that started out early in the eastern TX Panhandle produced some heavy rainfall as well, as these storms moved slowly and eventually merged into one large storm moving south through the rest of the eastern TX Panhandle.
episodes.183061: Several rounds of thunderstorms impacted the combined OK/TX Panhandles during the early evening hours of the 5th and going through into the early AM hours of the 6th. First, in the eastern TX Panhandle. Then a complex came in from eastern New Mexico impacting the southwestern TX Panhandle. Another complex then came in from SE Colorado and SW Kansas impacting the northern combined OK/TX Panhandles. Severe winds occurred with these storms and one instance of 1 hail also occurred. The strongest winds were with the complex that came into the OK Panhandle with winds upwards of 70 to 80 mph. The storms that started out early in the eastern TX Panhandle produced some heavy rainfall as well, as these storms moved slowly and eventually merged into one large storm moving south through the rest of the eastern TX Panhandle.
episodes.183165: A slow moving thunderstorm over Lake Charles produced isolated flooding.
episodes.183167: Weak upper-level disturbances migrated across South Florida, which including daytime heating, brought strong thunderstorms to the interior and Lake Okeechobee areas on July 6th.
episodes.183188: Melt water from the historic snowpack in the Sierra flooded a road.
episodes.183257: Severe thunderstorms produced very large hail in Lincoln County, ranging from 1 to 4 inches in diameter.  At least one spotter reported extensive hail damage to their home when it was struck by baseball size hail.  In  addition, two landspout tornadoes were observed in Adams and Arapahoe Counties.  One of the tornadoes picked up a 1400 pound disk and tossed it approximately 100 yards.
episodes.183302: A cold front pushed into the Mid-South during the afternoon and evening hours on July 5, 2023. The front interacted with an unstable airmass favorable for producing strong downdrafts. Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed along the front as it moved into areas along and north of I-40. A few of the storms produced damaging winds.
episodes.183343: Almost three inches of rain dumped in Monticello (Drew County) on the 6th, and high water flowed across Highway 278. The road had to be closed temporarily. It was the same story at Greenbrier (Faulkner County), with numerous roads under water.
episodes.183354: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours of July 6th, in an environment characterized by 800 to 1000 J/kg of downdraft CAPE.  This, plus sufficient dry air aloft, allowed for the development of downburst winds that produced isolated instances of wind damage.
episodes.183477: From the afternoon of July 6 on into the evening, isolated to scattered clusters of showers and thunderstorms impacted portions of northern Utah and southwest Wyoming, yielding a few strong to severe wind gusts.
episodes.183713: A thunderstorm produced large hail across Stanton County.
episodes.183812: An isolated thunderstorm produced some large hail across the Story and Big Horn areas.
episodes.183942: A shortwave moved across Wyoming. As it encountered more humid air east of the Bighorn Range, severe thunderstorms developed in Johnson and Natrona Counties. There were numerous reports of hail from nickel to golf ball size hail, including on Interstate 25 which slowed traffic for a time. In portions of Fremont and Sweetwater Counties, strong winds mixed to the surface and brought local high wind.
episodes.184126: Residual moisture from an incredibly anomalously wet June continues to moisten the lower levels aiding in ample amounts of instability. The northwest flow pattern created a lot of shear, which led to prolonged 3 day severe weather event over adjacent and eastern plains of southern Colorado.
episodes.184224: A cluster of strong thunderstorms brought damaging winds, torrential rainfall, and flash flooding to parts of northern Illinois during the afternoon and evening of July 5. Several rain gauges around the area recorded one to two inches of rain within a 30 minute period underneath some of these storms. The city of Chicago and its near-south and near-west suburbs were the areas hit hardest. Numerous reports were received of flooded roads, including a number of residential streets. Additionally, two firefighters were injured battling a fire caused by lightning striking a townhouse.
episodes.184268: Scattered storms developed each afternoon hours and a few became strong to severe which downed some trees.
episodes.184536: Lake Erie and northeast OH remained in the warm sector during the late morning through early evening hours of July 6th as a cold front drifted eastward across far-western Lake Erie and western OH. Clusters of multicell showers and thunderstorms well-ahead of the front persisted generally eastward over south-central Lake Erie and adjacent portions of northeast OH during the early afternoon. These showers and storms produced several gale-force peak convective wind gusts along the lakeshore. The showers and storms encountered moderate MUCAPE and effective bulk shear, respectively.
episodes.184538: Northwest Pennsylvania remained in the warm sector during the late morning through early evening hours of July 6th as a cold front drifted eastward across far-western Lake Erie and western OH. A cluster of multicell showers and thunderstorms well-ahead of the front persisted eastward in Crawford County, PA during the late afternoon and produced isolated straight-line convective wind damage. These showers and storms encountered moderate MUCAPE and effective bulk shear, respectively.
episodes.184610: An unstable and uncapped environment was in place ahead of a weak boundary. An area of thunderstorms moved into NW Indiana, but was weakening. A lone thunderstorm developed in southwestern St. Joseph county and tracked quickly NE over South Bend with a wet microburst producing a 79 mph wind gust at South Bend Airport as well as damage in the area.
episodes.184863: Widely scattered thunderstorms developed along the Crystal Coast during the overnight hours on July 5th. These thunderstorm then strengthened and became strong to severe at times as they tracked into the Pamlico Sound and the offshore waters along the Crystal Coast during the early morning hours of July 6th.
episodes.185215: Scattered storms developed during the afternoon and a few storms became strong.
episodes.186194: A cluster of strong thunderstorms brought torrential rainfall and gusty winds over southern Lake Michigan during the afternoon and evening of the 5th.
